key_insight: A temporal deep learning model that analyzes longitudinal OCT visits can predict when dry AMD will progress from no GA to GA and from non-central GA to central GA over 2–6 years.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help identify patients at higher risk of meaningful geographic atrophy progression earlier, supporting closer monitoring and research planning.
method: Encoded OCT B-scan volumes into visit-level features using pretrained ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16 models.
Modeled the sequence of visits with RNN, LSTM, or Transformer architectures, with optional time-gap ({Delta}t) inputs.
Evaluated separate prediction horizons from 2 to 6 years using patient-level 80/20 splits and multiple random seeds.
evidence_signal: In 91 patients and 455 OCT volumes, performance was strong, with ROC-AUC 0.84–0.94 for NGA-to-GA prediction at 2–4 years and up to 0.95–0.96 for NCGA-to-CGA prediction at 4–5 years.
watch_item: The study is retrospective and single-center, so external validation is needed before considering real-world deployment.
paper_title: Sequential Deep Learning to Predict Non-Central to Central Geographic Atrophy Progression from OCT Imaging
